core_obligations: Set up the computation (proof lines 1587-1619): using the cofinality of Cov, write H^p(U, F) as the colimit of the Cech cohomologies of the coverings in Cov, so that the hypothesis that those Cech groups vanish for p greater than zero gives the vanishing of H^p(U, F) for U in B.

Induction step (proof lines 1622-1647): for the general degree the author embeds F into an injective sheaf, uses the long exact cohomology sequence of the resulting short exact sequence, and combines the vanishing of the higher Cech groups with the induction hypothesis to deduce the vanishing in the next degree.
The counted proof also records the variant nature of the statement, since it is the version of a known result adapted from the chapter Cohomology to the present collection of coverings.
proof_roadmap: Replace cohomology by the Cech cohomology of a cofinal system of coverings, using the hypotheses on B and Cov.
The hypothesis that those Cech groups vanish in positive degrees then gives the vanishing for the objects of B.
For higher degrees, embed the sheaf into an injective and use the long exact sequence together with the induction hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a vanishing criterion for the cohomology of an abelian sheaf on a site in terms of the vanishing of Cech cohomology for a collection of coverings which is cofinal in each object of a subset B (statement lines 1564-1585). The proof first replaces cohomology by the Cech cohomology of that collection, using cofinality (proof lines 1587-1619), and then handles the general degree by embedding the sheaf into an injective, applying the long exact cohomology sequence and using the induction hypothesis (proof lines 1622-1647). The non-formal content is the reduction to the Cech computation together with the degree induction. The claim is H2: two steps, both written out, and the statement is explicitly marked by the author as a variant of a known result.
